x: Sexton and Marshall running for their school, again completed a double for the first two places in the 100 and 220 yards and the school also won both the relay races.

In the Junior 4 x 110 yards relay our team comprising: Marshall, Tebbutt, Rae and Sexton, in that order, won their heat in 45,5 secs. In the final they drew lane 4, on the outside, and thanks to an almost super human effort by Alan Sexton, after bad baton handling earlier, won in 45.3 secs.
Discus: 1st, Abbott, 125 ft. 10½ ins.; 2nd, A. Sexton, 102 ft. 2½ ins.; 4th, Marshall, 87 ft. 1¾ ins. Weight: 3rd, Law, 33 ft. 5½ ins.; 4th, Morrison, 28 ft. 3½ ins.

Sexton won his first heat in 24.1; Tebbutt won his first heat in 24.6; Picton, Marshall and Rae were each second in their heats. Sexton beat Marshall in the second round in 23.6; Picton won his second round in 23.9.

Match Events: 100 yards: 1, Marshall, 10.9 secs.; 3rd, Rae. 220 yards: Picton (W. and B.), 25 secs.; 2nd, Law (B); 3rd, Marsh (B). 440 yards: Morrison (B), 54.7 secs.; 3rd, Tranter (B). 880 yards: 1st, Tranter (B); Chitty (B). 1 mile: 2nd, Hazel.

Bishop, 2 min. 10 secs. 1 mile: Herbert, 4 min. 52 secs., 3rd, Short Relay (4 x half a lap), 1st, Epsom; 2nd, Bels. (Grimshaw, Simmons, Walden and Broadbent); 3rd, Bel, Juniors (Marshall, Baker, Mullen, Sexton).
Marshall and Mullen also competed and were each placed fourth in their heats both clocking 23.7 secs. Morrison was fourth in his 440 yards heat in 55 secs.

Marshall, 10.8 secs. 100 yards (Seniors).—Grosvenor Cup: 1st, Broadbent; 2nd, Sexton; 3rd, Lowers (holder), 10.3 secs. 220 yards (under 19).—Ricketts Cup: 1st Marshall; 2nd, Mullen; 3rd, Picton, 23.7 secs. 220 yards.—Elsie Gordon Cup: 1st, Sexton; 2nd, Broadbent; 3rd, Walden, 22.8 secs. 880 yards (under 19).—W.

Frank Kemp made a double of it by winning the 220 yards Junior race, beating Dave Marshall, who is the Surrey champion at this distance. Alan Sexton was defending his 220 yards senior title, but owing to his service in the R.A.F. was not up to last year's form and was beaten into second place by D.
At the Saturday fixture we were pleased to see Dave Marshall, our old Junior sprint champion, make a welcome reappearance, and he won the 100 yds., with T.
Our team of Holtum, Marshall, Walden and Mayers were drawn on the outside and with Marshall being short of training we could only finish in 6th place.
